title: How Replicable Are Statistically Significant Findings?
abstract: arXiv:2608.23257v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In the empirical sciences, significance thresholds often determine whether findings are treated as evidence of an effect. This paper studies how likely findings that just meet conventional significance thresholds are to remain significant in replications of the same sample size. To answer this question, we estimate the expected replication probability conditional on a given p-value among published studies for experimental economics, psychology, and social science. We validate this measure by showing it accurately predicts actual replication outcomes, outperforming prediction markets. A finding with a p-value of 0.05 has an expected replication probability ranging from 0.10 to 0.25 across fields. Low replicability reflects low power in original studies rather than publication bias. We then develop a nonparametric estimator and apply it to economics literatures that use larger samples, finding higher but still low replication probabilities

translated_title: 统计显著发现的可复制性有多高？
translated_abstract: 在实证科学中，显著性阈值往往决定研究结果是否被视为效应的证据。本文研究了那些刚好达到传统显著性阈值的研究发现，在相同样本量的复制研究中，有多大可能继续保持显著。为回答此问题，我们基于给定p值，估计了实验经济学、心理学和社会科学中已发表研究的预期复制概率。我们通过展示该指标能准确预测实际复制结果（优于预测市场）来验证其有效性。p值为0.05的发现，其预期复制概率在不同领域中介于0.10到0.25之间。低复制性反映了原始研究的低统计功效，而非发表偏倚。我们随后开发了一种非参数估计器，并将其应用于使用较大样本的经济学文献，发现复制概率有所提高但仍较低。
tldr: 本文发现，p值恰为0.05的统计显著发现，其复制概率在不同学科中仅为10%至25%，且低复制性主要源于原始研究的低功效，而非发表偏倚。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that findings with a p-value of 0.05 have replication probabilities of only 10%-25% across fields, with low replicability driven by low power in original studies rather than publication bias.
